description:
Create a delegation (Proof of Delegation): a control-proven domain authorizes a typed url/purl artifact and receives a publishable signed token. The attestation is that the domain's controller authorized this artifact — nothing more; it says nothing about the artifact or the business behind it. Each mint is a billable proof. A requested lifetime longer than the control proof's remainder is rejected, never truncated. The result carries the publishable token AND the DERIVED effective_status/is_valid — the same pair the list and get tools return, so the shape does not depend on which verb produced it.

ACCESS: needs a Proof account. Set PROOF_API_KEY and restart this server, then call this tool again. start_login does NOT open this tool.

control_proof.description: Public handle (ph_ctl_<32 hex>) of YOUR active domain control proof

type.description: Identifier type: https URL or package URL (purl)

expires_in.description: Lifetime in seconds (must not exceed the control proof's remainder)

name: create_delegation

control_proof.description: The control proof handle this delegation points down to

delegation_id.description: Stable public handle (`ph_dlg_<32 hex>`) — also the token's `sub`, and accepted by the proof status endpoint

effective_status.description: DERIVED liveness, computed at read time from BOTH clocks that govern a delegation: the control proof it stands on (cascade rule a — revoked, suspended or expired flows through) and its own `expires_at` (rule b — effective expiry is the earlier of the two). Either one running out reports `expired` here while the delegation's own `status` stays untouched. This is the field to render — `status` alone would show a live badge on a delegation every verifier already rejects

expires_at.description: Never later than the control proof's own expiry at issuance (effective expiry is min of the two)

is_valid.description: True only when `effective_status` is `active`. It is a restatement of that field, not a second opinion: expiry is decided once, inside the derivation above

principal.description: The proven domain that authorized the delegate — derived from the control proof, never client input

scope.description: Deprecated. Delegation schema 2.0 carries no scope; this array stays for the SDKs released before it: the scope a delegation issued before schema 2.0 was stored with, otherwise empty. Removed in the next major version.

status.description: The owner's OWN record — whether they revoked this delegation themselves. Nothing else writes it: neither the control proof dying nor this delegation's own lifetime running out. Liveness is DERIVED and reported separately as `effective_status`. This stored field is also what `?status=` filters on

token.description: The signed delegation JWT — the PUBLISHABLE artifact (publish it in your MCP server card under `_meta` → `holdings.proof/delegation`). Same key, algorithm and JWKS as proof tokens
